Hi Logan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP submission last week. Our legal + data protection teams have a couple of follow-ups specifically around the DPA annex and the cross-border transfer / DPF evidence you referenced. High-level asks below:

1) Attenuated access design: can you provide a short architecture note that explains how Redwood limits access to customer data when serving EU-origin requests from US-hosted inference? We need to understand logical isolation, KV cache segregation, and any tokenization or pseudonymization layers you use.

2) Subprocessor mapping: a table/list of subprocessors used for processing and any planned changes in the next 12 months. We need to show which subprocessors have access to key material (if any) and where key management services are located.

3) DPF evidence: specific artifacts (logs/diagrams/configs) you can provide for an EU-US DPF demonstration — examples: flow diagrams, WAF/NSG rules that prevent egress, key rotation schedule, SOC2 sections mapping. Which artifacts are redacted vs. shareable?

Given timeline on our side, it would be ideal to get an initial evidence package and DPA annex draft by next week. Can you confirm availability and whether you need an NDA amendment or further POI?

Best,

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. We can deliver an initial evidence bundle and a DPA annex draft by next Thursday (2028-11-30). Quick answers and proposal below, and I attached the pack we referenced in the RFP (redwood-dpf-evidence-pack.pdf) plus the current DPA annex draft (dpa-annex-draft-v3.docx) for your legal team to review.

Short answers:
- Attenuated access: Redwood implements per-tenant logical isolation (separate runtime tenant IDs, per-tenant KV namespaces) and request-scoped credentials for model servers. We operate an ingress-only model for text generation: customer payloads are processed in-memory, KV cache entries are tagged with tenant IDs and encrypted at rest. We never persist full unredacted customer prompts to long-term storage unless explicitly configured for logging or audit — all retention is configurable per-customer.
- Key management: customer data-in-flight is protected by TLS; at-rest encryption uses AES-256 with KMS-backed envelope keys. For Private deployments customers can supply their own KMS (bring-your-own-key).
- Subprocessors: see the attached evidence pack; summary: cloud infra providers (AWS, GCP) for compute, managed KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) depending on region, a metrics/observability vendor (Prometheus/Thanos managed partner), and a logging aggregator (log-ops vendor) with limited access. We can provide a redacted mapping that shows process-level access and full mapping under NDA.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll host a 45-minute call with our security engineer and my legal lead to walk through the design and artifacts. Suggested slots: Wed 11/29 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 11/30 09:00-10:00 PT.
2) I'll prepare a short architecture note focused on attenuated access (2 pages) plus a redacted subprocessor table and the list of artifacts we can share immediately vs. under NDA.
3) If you need targeted artifacts (e.g., key rotation logs or WAF rule snippet), let me know which specific items are priority so we can gather them.

Attached: redwood-dpf-evidence-pack.pdf, dpa-annex-draft-v3.docx

Logan / Monica — quick internal note so we can be aligned before the call with MedNova. Please keep this internal (will quote externally later).

1) Attenuated access design (technical bullets for architecture note):
- Tenant isolation: each customer gets a runtime tenant id; model servers enforce tenant-scoped namespaces for KV cache and ephemeral request contexts.
- KV cache: encrypted at rest with per-tenant envelope keys; caches are sharded by tenant and TTLs are short (default 1 hour), configurable. No cross-tenant cache reads.
- Logging: by default we retain only hashed request identifiers in observability pipelines; full request payloads are stored only when customer enables strict audit logging (explicit opt-in) and by default are redacted before any persistent storage.
- Admin access: role-based access with just-in-time approval for debug sessions; session recordings and access audit logs are captured and immutable.
- Network egress control: for hosted deployments traffic egress is restricted by region-specific VPC egress rules; EU-origin requests routed to EU edge region when configured, otherwise routed through US compute with contractual safeguards.

2) Subprocessor mapping notes:
- We should produce two tables: minimal shareable (vendor name + function + country) and full (includes contract tier and access level) under NDA.
- Highlight KMS locations: US-EAST-1 (primary) and EU-WEST-1 (replica) depending on customer's provisioning.

3) Artifacts we can deliver quickly: architecture diagram (attestation), redacted subprocessor list, sample KMS policy (redacted), WAF rule sample, SOC2 mapping extract. Anything requiring raw logs or non-redacted key material requires an Execution SLA and NDA.

I'll draft the 2-page architecture note and sample artifacts today; Logan, if you can confirm the call slot we can lock the calendar.

—Karthik
Senior Security Engineer

Elena / DPO team —

Following up with the deliverables we discussed. Attached is a redacted evidence bundle (redwood-dpf-evidence-pack.pdf) and our working DPA annex draft (dpa-annex-draft-v3.docx). Below is a concise technical summary that you can share with legal/DP teams; Ive kept any sensitive implementation detail redacted in the pack and note where full artifacts are available under NDA.

Technical summary (one-page):
- Data handling model: Request payloads are processed in-memory by per-tenant model runners. Ephemeral KV caches are tenant-scoped, encrypted at rest (AES-256), and keyed via KMS envelope keys. Default cache TTL is 1 hour.
- Pseudonymization & retention: We do offer a pseudonymization option that replaces direct identifiers before processing; retention windows for any persisted artifacts are configurable per contract (default: 30 days for diagnostic logs, 0 days for raw prompts unless explicitly enabled).
- Admin and debug access: All human access is mediated via RBAC with JIT approval; debug sessions are scoped and recorded. Access logs are immutable and retained per the customer retention policy.
- Subprocessors (summary): cloud compute providers (US/EU), KMS providers (region-dependent), metrics/monitoring partner, and a logging aggregator. Exported mapping: shareable redacted table attached; full mapping requires an NDA.
- Key management: envelope encryption; optional BYOK for Private deployments. Key rotation schedule: quarterly rotations, documented in the evidence pack (redacted rotation tokens omitted).
- Controls to prevent unauthorized export: egress filtering at VPC-level, egress ACLs, and WAF rules; for especially sensitive customers we support static routes that avoid cross-border egress by pinning compute to EU zones or Private deployment.

Requested artifacts included in the attached pack (redacted):
- Architecture diagram (attestation)
- Redacted subprocessor mapping (vendor + function + country)
- KMS policy sample (redacted)
- SOC2 control mapping extract (relevant sections)
- WAF rule sample and network egress configuration snippets

Artifacts available under NDA / contract amendment:
- Non-redacted subprocessor mapping with contract tiers and access levels
- KMS rotation logs and raw audit trails

- Proposed call: Wed 11/29 10:00-10:45 PT (security + legal + DPO). If that works Ill send a Teams invite and include our security engineer (Karthik) and contracts lead (Monica).
